description: Port ONIX (open-source depletion code) to supply the MSRE depletion + fission-product inventory source term. Provides the actinide + FP isotopic evolution that feeds the FP-migration chemistry. Consider folding into outram-mc-libs (which already has a depletion path) vs a dedicated crate — decide in design. Complements a CRAM (Chebyshev Rational Approximation) Bateman-solver port from OpenMC (MIT) and ENDF/B decay + fission-yield data into njoy-outram-park-fork (separate tasks). LICENSE: ONIX believed GPL — verify upstream LICENSE and confirm GPLv3-compatibility (not GPL-2-only) before porting; keep provenance header. Pure-Rust, no FFI/PETSc/MPI. Untrusted AI-assisted draft pending human V&V.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: License due-diligence (2026-08-04): ONIX = jlanversin/ONIX, MIT/X license -> GPLv3-COMPATIBLE. CLEARED to port (keep MIT provenance). Python 3. Bonus findings: (1) ONIX already implements a CRAM (Chebyshev Rational Approximation) Bateman solver + OpenMC coupling + stand-alone precomputed mode -> porting ONIX subsumes the separately-mooted OpenMC-CRAM task; (2) an MSR-specific branch exists (Mhelhareef/ONIX @ MSR) directly relevant to MSRE depletion.

description:
DONE 2026-08-12 (this bead records the work and the one honesty caveat).

Htr10ReactorVesselVisual now draws its control rods in the SIDE REFLECTOR annulus -- ten borings in the graphite in the real machine, so never through the pebble bed. Each drawn boring is helium-tinted and always visible; the absorber hangs from its top to the drawn depth with a lighter tip cap, and a steel drive shaft runs to the head penetration so a fully withdrawn bank still reads as a parked rod rather than nothing.

Animation: animation/control_rod_drive.rs (egui-free, Android-clean) holds ControlRodDrive, which slews the DRAWN insertion fraction toward the commanded one at speed/stroke per second. components/control_rod_drive.rs persists it across repaints in egui's per-context store keyed by a caller-chosen Id, since widgets are rebuilt every frame. Wired in examples/htgr_sim_v1/app/schematic.rs off HtgrSnapshot::control_rod_insertion_fraction.

OPEN HONESTY CAVEAT -- the drive SPEED is ILLUSTRATIVE, not sourced. No published HTR-10 rod drive speed was found in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10-plant-data.md, htr10-neutronics.md, or crates/kovan-literature/open/ (searched 2026-08-12). The value used is stroke / 20 s = 0.0985 m/s, chosen purely so the travel is watchable, and is labelled ILLUSTRATIVE in htr10_illustrative_rod_drive_speed(), in the widget docs and in the example's module docs. The STROKE (1.97 m, the published mean pebble bed height) IS sourced. If anyone finds a real drive speed, replace it and cite it -- that is the follow-up this bead should be reopened for.
title: htgr_sim_v1: HTR-10 side-reflector control rods drawn + animated

description:
Bring htgr_sim_v1 up to the standard the CIET educational simulator v2 sets: a real GUI, an OPC-UA server exposing plant state, and a client that reads it.

TARGET SHAPE, from src/bin/ciet_educational_simulator_v2/: main.rs + cli.rs + headless.rs + opcua_startup.rs + a simulator subdir, backed by an OPC-UA layer.

CURRENT STATE (46482b4): htgr_sim_v1 is an EXAMPLE, not a bin — examples/htgr_sim_v1/{app/{mod,panels,schematic,state}.rs, physics/{kinetics,primary_loop,secondary_loop}.rs}. Working GUI, 12 passing tests, honest lumped physics with explicit 'what is real / what is illustrative' contracts. No OPC-UA at all.

THE ARCHITECTURAL DECISION: src/ciet_opcua/ is 4206 lines, heavily CIET-specific (109 CIET references in server.rs, 90 in node_map.rs), but its transport scaffolding is generic — OpcuaServerConfig, OpcuaEndpointInfo, OpcuaServerHandle, OpcuaServerError, spawn_opcua_server_thread, plus pki_paths.rs (333 lines) and discovery.rs (631 lines).

Extract the generic layer so CIET and HTGR each supply their own node map and state, rather than copy-pasting. Extraction is right — a second simulator is exactly when duplication becomes permanent — but it refactors WORKING, TESTED code (CIET v2 has 37 passing tests) and must not regress them.

SEPARATE DECISION, not assumed here: htgr_sim_v1 is a PRISMATIC-BLOCK HTGR today, not a pebble bed (docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md). A true HTR-10 core is a rewrite, not a retune. The GUI/OPC-UA work is orthogonal and can proceed either way.
title: htgr_sim_v1: full HTR-10 simulator — GUI + OPC-UA server and client

description: v2's physics is a cp -ar port of v1's educational_ciet_loop_version_4. The maintainer has done validation work on v1's physics, so the open question is PORT EQUIVALENCE, not the physics itself. Methodology: run v1 (tuas example) and v2 (DT engine bin) from identical initial state with identical control inputs and a fixed timestep, dump CIETState/CietState each step to CSV, and compare. Pass criterion: temperatures agree to solver round-off (suggest 1e-9 degC) over >=2000 s of simulated time. Until this runs, v2 must NOT be described as validated -- only as a faithful port of validated physics.
title: V&V: verify CIET v2 physics port reproduces v1 bit-for-bit
